In Memory of Andrew Faught

Every Legacy Has a Story.

Andrew John “Drew” Faught (February 22, 1997 – April 8, 2024) grew up in Morris, Illinois. Long before he wore the uniform of the Illinois Department of Corrections, he was an athlete who loved competition, teamwork, and pushing himself to become stronger.

Drew played youth football with the Morris Chiefs and later played football and wrestled at Morris Community High School. Wearing #78, he played offensive and defensive line. His 2014 varsity football statistics record 38 tackles and 7 sacks in 12 games. His love of fitness continued through weightlifting and training.

Drew dedicated six years to the Illinois Department of Corrections. He served at Pontiac Correctional Center, earned promotion to sergeant, and became a member of the Tactical Response Team (TRT). He carried strength, discipline, and a commitment to his fellow officers into his work.

On April 8, 2024, Drew was heading to Lawrence Correctional Center when he was tragically in an accident which took his life.

Drew’s service was recognized with Illinois flags flown at half-staff in April 2024, an Illinois Senate memorial resolution in 2025, and recognition among fallen officers at the Illinois Police Officers Memorial. His name was also included in the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial’s 2025 roll call.

But Drew was far more than a jersey number, a statistic, a rank, or an honor. He was a son, a brother, an uncle, a teammate, a coworker, and a friend. His family and the people who knew him carry forward the life, laughter, strength, and love he shared.

AJ Legacy Apparel was created to honor his life through designs rooted in strength, service, family, and perseverance. Proceeds from qualifying Limited Edition memorial merchandise are designated to support Concerns of Police Survivors (C.O.P.S.); the donation calculation and terms will be disclosed before sales begin.

Until Tomorrow.

From graduation, football, and training to family Christmases and Police Week in Washington, D.C., these photographs celebrate Drew’s life and the people who carry his legacy forward. Concerns of Police Survivors (C.O.P.S.) helped Drew’s family travel to Police Week and made sure they were cared for throughout the experience.
